subtitle: A request for references on data communications and communications theory.

tldr.problem: J. Bouknight asks for reference material in two subject areas.
tldr.mechanism: The note asks technical liaison contacts to send as many references as they can to the Center for Advanced Computation at the University of Illinois.
tldr.outcome: The one-page RFC is a request and does not describe what materials were received.

today: The unit metadata records RFC 81 as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its text is a request for reference information dated December 1970.

sections.title: References Requested
sections.content:
J. Bouknight asks technical liaison contacts to send as many references as they can on data communications and communications theory.

The note does not state why the references are needed or report any response to the request.
sections.plainLanguage: The author asks other sites to send available references on two topics. The note does not say what response the request received.

sections.title: Where to Send the Material
sections.content: The mailing address is the Center for Advanced Computation, University of Illinois, 168 Engineering Research Laboratory, Urbana, Illinois 61801.
sections.plainLanguage: The note gives a postal address at the University of Illinois for sending the references.

sections.title: Scope of the Note
sections.content: RFC 81 is a brief administrative request. It identifies the subjects for the references and gives a mailing address, without defining a technical protocol or a process for organizing the material.
sections.plainLanguage: This short RFC asks for reference material and tells readers where to mail it. It does not set out a technical design.
